narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To demonstrate that private school participation in Britain is heavily concentrated among the highest income earners.

units.meaning: Private school participation reaches its highest relative level at the end of its series (x=1220.0), with relative_value 1.0332 (value 0.6199).

basis.note: also value=0.6199; maximum of this series

accepted_routes: Private school participation peaks at about 1.03 on the normalized scale at the final point.
The highest private school participation value is 1.0332 (0.6199 in the value column), occurring at x=1220.0.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The Private school participation series must visibly attain its maximum at its final plotted point.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause about intakes being dominated by the very wealthy
units.reviewer_question: Should the video be required to show the final point as the maximum of the private school participation series?

units.meaning: Private school participation rises from 0.1000 to 1.0332 relative_value (0.0600 to 0.6199 value) between x=1143.3 and x=1220.0, a factor of about 10.3.
accepted_routes: The private school participation series increases roughly tenfold from its first to last plotted point.
It grows from 0.10 to 1.03 on the relative scale, about a 10.3x increase.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The Private school participation series must show a steep upward trend from its first to last point, consistent with a tenfold increase.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause about private school participation being dominated by the wealthy
units.reviewer_question: Is the tenfold increase from start to end of the private school participation series a required takeaway?

units.meaning: The Richest 10% series peaks at 0.1667 relative_value (0.1000 value) at x=1117.7.

basis.note: also value=0.1000; maximum of this series

accepted_routes: The Richest 10% series reaches its highest relative value, 0.1667 (0.1000 in the value column), at x=1117.7.
The richest 10% line peaks at about 0.17 on the relative scale.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The Richest 10% series must visibly reach its maximum at x=1117.7 before any later point.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause about the very wealthy
units.reviewer_question: Should the video be required to identify the peak of the Richest 10% series?

units.meaning: At x=1143.3, the last Richest 10% point and the first Private school participation point have the same relative_value 0.1000 (value 0.0600).
accepted_routes: The two series meet at x=1143.3 with the same relative value of 0.1000 (0.0600 in the value column).
At the shared x-coordinate, both entities have equal relative_value 0.1000.
units.visual_evidence_rule: At the shared x position, the Richest 10% and Private school participation series must visibly coincide or cross at the same value.
units.temporal_anchor: the transition between discussing the wealthy and private school participation
units.reviewer_question: Should the video explicitly show the point where the two series meet and share the same value?

units.meaning: The maximum relative_value of Private school participation (1.0332 at x=1220.0) is about 6.2 times the maximum relative_value of Richest 10% (0.1667 at x=1117.7).
accepted_routes: The peak private school participation relative value is roughly six times the peak Richest 10% relative value.
Private school participation maxes at 1.0332, while Richest 10% maxes at 0.1667, a ratio of about 6.2.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The maximum of the Private school participation series must be visibly much higher than the maximum of the Richest 10% series.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause about intakes being dominated by the very wealthy
units.reviewer_question: Should the video compare the peak levels of the two series, or is that an invalid cross-entity comparison?

optional_valid: The Richest 10% series declines from its peak 0.1667 at x=1117.7 to 0.1000 at x=1143.3.
The Private school participation series has an intermediate value 0.9167 at x=1207.2, just before its maximum.
The Richest 10% series has a local low of 0.0332 at several early points.
unsupported_to_avoid: Stating that private school participation is a percentage, count, or dollar amount, since the unit column is blank.
Claiming that funding cuts caused the private school participation pattern.
Extrapolating the Private school participation trend beyond x=1220.0 or the Richest 10% trend before x=120.0.
Stating that the Richest 10% group has the highest private school participation, because the table does not cross-tabulate income groups with participation.
notes: The table has no unit column, so all numbers are treated as relative/table values rather than percentages or counts. The key contrast is between the Richest 10% series peaking at 0.1667 and Private school participation rising to 1.0332.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
